explanation: Retrospective detector of the vocabulary of abstract construal - the words a written text uses to frame, ask about, classify and organize its subject rather than to name concrete things and physical events. It peaks (0.9-1.6) on (i) the interrogative words what, why and how (and less reliably whether, where, when, which) opening a question or an embedded question ('she explained how...' 1.20, 'we know what you mean' 1.0-1.3, 'it is uncertain whether...' 0.77); (ii) the links of, for, about and on when they carry the complement of an abstract head ('a common method of raising money' 1.56, 'several reasons for the delay' 1.54, 'types of soil' 1.0, 'tips for saving money' 0.94, 'the criteria for the award' 0.69, 'an overview of' 0.84) but only weakly (0-0.3) when the same links attach to a concrete, partitive, temporal or proper head ('a loaf of bread' 0.0, 'ten minutes for the bus' 0.2-0.3, 'for three hours' 0.0, 'the College of' 0.0); (iii) the verbs of describing, explaining, analysing and organizing (describe, explain, discuss, suggest, recommend, consider, examine, compare, present) at 0.6-1.5, with the abstract head nouns they take (aspect, method, reasons, criteria, overview, type, framework, view, information, research, quality) firing more weakly and unevenly on their own (0.2-0.95: overview and aspect strongest, method and results weakest) and clearly when a link or an exposition verb sits beside them; and (iv) the connectives and quantifiers of written argument (although, while, because, however, moreover, thus, therefore, still, even, only, such, both, each, several, most, all, another, indeed) at 0.5-1.2, and 'and'/'or' where it coordinates abstract words ('research and', 'quality and', 'cultural and' 0.6-0.9) but not concrete or human ones ('children and', 'men and' 0.0). It stays in the 0-0.4 band on narration and physical procedure - personal pronouns, the definite article, concrete nouns for objects, substances, places and people (roof, tiles, rope, bread, oven, soil, ice), physical verbs (leaked, carried, poured, hammered, washed, sat) and measurements - and because a text's first token is read with no context whatever, its first-position value is a bare-token prior (high on A/An, numerals, what/why/how/whether/when, although, this, about; near zero on he/she/they/my, the, in/at), so predictions of inactivity are for the text from its second token onward.
